title: multilevel undo
name: Multilevel undo
rule: Let the user reverse a series of actions, not only the last one.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Doing Things — Multilevel Undo (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: More than the last action can be reversed.
fail_when: No undo, or only last-action undo.
overview: People can reverse a series of actions, not only the last one.
apply_when: Editing flows where mistakes stack across multiple steps.
not_when: Single-step views where last-action undo already covers all risk.
agent_hint: Support multilevel undo so more than the last action can be reversed.
description: Undo should reverse a series of actions, not only the last one, so stacked mistakes remain recoverable. Last-action-only undo, or no undo at all, leaves earlier mistakes stuck after a longer editing session. Provide multilevel undo in multi-step editing where history accumulates. A single atomic action may only need one undo step; depth matters when several changes stack.
